Project: /root/bench-runs/h5-a984a158 (Node 24, ESM, no deps; NEVER npm install; Node built-ins only). Write node:test tests only. Do NOT change lib/, server.mjs, README.md. Create ONLY test/import-checks.test.mjs (another coder writes test/import-success.test.mjs and test/amounts.test.mjs in parallel; do not touch them). Run with `cd /root/bench-runs/h5-a984a158 && node --test test/import-checks.test.mjs`, then `npm test`. Load skill tdd-workflow if available.

Rules: copy style of test/api.test.mjs (no semicolons, single quotes, `import { test } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`). Use test/helpers.mjs `withApp(async call => ...)`; `call(method, path, body)` returns {status, body, text}; a string body is sent raw (use for raw JSON like `4.350`). Assert full reply bodies with assert.deepEqual — exact equality, never prefix/regex/partial. No console.log. Functions < 50 lines; file <= 400 lines — use small helper functions (e.g. `importTo(call, body, group='trip')`, `expectProblems(call, entries, problems, extra={})`, `assertNothingSaved(call)`) and table-driven loops with a message argument naming the case. Read README.md section "## Import" and lib/import.mjs, lib/validate.mjs, lib/expenses.mjs.

Fixture: group trip = {id:'trip', name:'Ski trip', members:['Ann','Ben','Cara']}; valid expense E = {type:'expense', description:'Hotel', payer:'Ann', amount:90}; valid payment P = {type:'payment', from:'Ben', to:'Ann', amount:30}.

"Nothing saved" check (use after every 400/422/404 case group): GET /groups/trip/expenses body deepEqual {expenses:[...whatever existed before]}, GET payments likewise, and finally a POST /groups/trip/expenses gets the expected next id and POST payments the expected next id (do this once at the end of a test, since it creates data).

Tests to write (each spec line needs a test a plausible wrong implementation fails):
1. 413: entries array whose JSON is > 10 KB (e.g. 50 expenses with description 'x'.repeat(200)... make sure >10240 bytes) → 413 {error:'body too large'}; nothing saved.
2. Non-object body: '[1]' and 'null' and '"x"' raw → 400 {error:'body must be a JSON object'}; '{"entries": ' → 400 {error:'invalid JSON'}.
3. Unknown group → 404 {error:'not found'} even when the body is otherwise bad: {entries:[E]}, {foo:1}, {entries:[]}, {entries:[E], dry_run:'yes'}, {entries:[null]}. Also group id that is invalid format like 'NOPE'.
4. 400 order and exact messages (all with group trip existing):
   - {entries:[E], foo:1} → 'unknown field foo'; {zed:1, entries:[E], alpha:2} → 'unknown field zed' (first in Object.keys order, NOT alphabetical); unknown field beats bad entries: {entries:'x', foo:1} → 'unknown field foo'; {dry_run:'x', bar:1} → 'unknown field bar'. Case sensitive: {Entries:[E]} → 'unknown field Entries'. Field '__proto__' sent raw as '{"entries":[...],"__proto__":1}' → 'unknown field __proto__'.
   - entries: missing key, null, {}, 'abc', [] (0 items), 51 items → 'entries must be an array of 1 to 50 items'; 1 item and 50 items (50 distinct valid payments, or expenses with distinct descriptions) pass (status 201). entries check beats dry_run: {entries:[], dry_run:'x'} → entries message.
   - dry_run: 'true', 1, 0, null, 'false', [] , {} → 'dry_run must be true or false'; dry_run check beats skip_recorded: {entries:[E], dry_run:null, skip_recorded:null} → dry_run message.
   - skip_recorded: 'true', 1, null → 'skip_recorded must be true or false'.
   - A 400 also beats entry problems: {entries:[null], dry_run:'x'} → 400 dry_run message (not 422).
5. 422 shape: exactly {error:'import rejected', problems:[{index, rule}, ...]} sorted by index, one item per bad entry (good entries not listed). Use a mixed list e.g. [E, null, P, {type:'x'}] → problems [{index:1,rule:'not-an-object'},{index:3,rule:'bad-type'}].
6. not-an-object: null, [], [E], 5, 'expense', true → not-an-object.
7. bad-type: {} (missing type), {type:null}, {type:'Expense'}, {type:'refund'}, {type:['expense']}, and {description:'Hotel', payer:'Ann', amount:90} → bad-type. bad-type beats unknown-field: {type:'x', foo:1} → bad-type.
8. unknown-field: expense with `from:'Ann'` → unknown-field; expense with `foo:1`; payment with `description:'x'`; payment with `split:['Ann']`; payment with `payer:'Ann'`. unknown-field beats bad-description: {type:'expense', description:'', payer:'Ann', amount:90, foo:1} → unknown-field. Expense with all five keys valid (split:['Ann','Ben']) passes; payment with exactly four keys passes.
9. Expense rule order, each one entry: description '', '   ', missing, null, 5, 'x'.repeat(201) → bad-description; description '' AND payer 'Dan' → bad-description (order). payer 'Dan', 'ann' (case), missing, null → bad-payer; payer 'Dan' and amount 0 → bad-payer. amount 0, -1, 1.234, '90', null, missing, 1000000.01 → bad-amount; amount 0 and split [] → bad-amount. split null, [], ['Ann','Ann'], ['Dan'], 'Ann', [1] → bad-split. Boundary passes: description 'x'.repeat(200), amount 0.01, amount 1000000.
10. Payment rules: from 'Dan', null, missing → bad-from; from 'Dan' & to 'Dan' → bad-from; to 'Dan', missing, null → bad-to; to equals from ('Ben'→'Ben') → bad-to; to==from with amount 0 → bad-to (bad-to beats bad-amount); amount 0, '30', null, missing, 1.234 → bad-amount. from 'ben' (wrong case) → bad-from.
11. duplicate: [E, E] → [{index:1,rule:'duplicate'}]; [E, E, E] → indexes 1 and 2 duplicate; description 'Taxi' vs '  taxi ' → duplicate; 'Hotel' vs 'HOTEL' duplicate; ' Hotel\t' vs 'hotel' duplicate (trim removes NBSP/tab); 'Café' vs 'CAFÉ' duplicate; amount sent raw: `{"entries":[{"type":"expense","description":"Taxi","payer":"Ann","amount":4.35},{"type":"expense","description":"Taxi","payer":"Ann","amount":4.350}]}` → duplicate; different split ['Ann'] vs none → still duplicate; NOT duplicates (expect 201): different payer, different amount (4.35 vs 4.36), different description ('Hotel' vs 'Hotel 2', 'Hot el'), and identical payments [P, P, P] → 201 with 3 payments. An invalid earlier expense does NOT make a later identical valid one a duplicate: [{...E, split:[]}, E] → only [{index:0, rule:'bad-split'}]; similarly [{...E, foo:1}, E] → only index 0 unknown-field. A duplicate entry that ALSO has an earlier-rule error reports the earlier rule: [E, {...E, split:['Dan']}] → [{index:1,rule:'bad-split'}].
12. already-recorded: POST /groups/trip/expenses {description:'Hotel', payer:'Ann', amount:90} first, then import [E] → [{index:0,rule:'already-recorded'}]; with description ' HOTEL ' also already-recorded; amount 90.5 not recorded (201). Expense of ANOTHER group doesn't count: create group 'flat' with same members, POST that expense to flat only, import [E] to trip → 201. A deleted expense doesn't count (POST then DELETE then import → 201). Duplicate beats already-recorded: with Hotel recorded, [E, E] skip_recorded false → [{index:0,rule:'already-recorded'},{index:1,rule:'duplicate'}]; skip_recorded true → 422 [{index:1,rule:'duplicate'}] (the skipped index 0 still counts as earlier). Also skip_recorded true does not skip other rules: [ {...E, payer:'Dan'} ] → 422 bad-payer.
13. dry_run gives the same errors: repeat a 400 case, a 422 case and a 404 case with dry_run:true and assert identical status+body.
14. Every 400/422/404 saves nothing (see "Nothing saved" above): include in at least one 400 and one 422 test, with pre-existing data (1 expense, 1 payment) and assert next ids (expense id 2, payment id 2).

If any test fails because the implementation disagrees with the README spec, do NOT change lib and do NOT weaken the test: keep the test, run the rest, and report the exact failing case (input, expected, actual). Report: file written, number of tests, pass/fail, any spec mismatch found.

content.content:
1	# Split service
2	
3	A small HTTP JSON service for groups of people who share expenses: who paid what, who owes whom. Node.js 24.2 or later, no dependencies.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	```
8	npm start
9	```
10	
11	| Env | Default | Meaning |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| `PORT` | `3000` | Port to listen on (127.0.0.1 only) |
14	| `DATA_FILE` | `groups.json` | Where the store is kept |
15	
16	On start it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. A missing data file is an empty store. Every change is written to the data file atomically (temp file, then rename), so a crash never leaves half a file.
17	
18	## Test
19	
20	```
21	npm test
22	```
23	
24	## API
25	
26	| Route | Body | Success | Errors |
27	|---|---|---|---|
28	| `POST /groups` | `{id, name, members}` | 201 the group | 400 invalid, 409 `group already exists` |
29	| `GET /groups/:id` | | 200 `{id, name, members}` | 404 |
30	| `POST /groups/:id/expenses` | `{description, payer, amount, split?}` | 201 the expense | 400 invalid, 404 unknown group |
31	| `GET /groups/:id/expenses` | | 200 `{expenses}`, sorted by id | 404 |
32	| `PATCH /groups/:id/expenses/:expenseId` | any of `{description, payer, amount, split}` | 200 the changed expense | 400 invalid, 404 |
33	| `DELETE /groups/:id/expenses/:expenseId` | | 204 | 404 |
34	| `POST /groups/:id/payments` | `{from, to, amount}` | 201 the payment | 400 invalid, 404 unknown group |
35	| `GET /groups/:id/payments` | | 200 `{payments}`, sorted by id | 404 |
36	| `GET /groups/:id/balances` | | 200 `{balances}` | 404 |
37	| `GET /groups/:id/settle-up` | | 200 `{payments}`, suggested, not recorded | 404 |
38	| `POST /groups/:id/import` | `{entries, dry_run?, skip_recorded?}` | 201 `{expenses, payments, skipped, balances}` (200 with `dry_run`) | 400 invalid, 404 unknown group, 413, 422 `import rejected` |
39	
40	An expense is shown as `{id, description, payer, amount, split, shares}`, where `shares` maps each name in `split` to what that person's part of the expense is. A payment is `{id, from, to, amount}`: `from` pays `to` back. Expense ids and payment ids each count up from 1 across all groups and are never reused.
41	
42	**Shares.** An expense is shared equally, in whole cents, by the people in its `split`. When the amount does not divide evenly, the first people in `split` pay one cent more each, so the shares always add up to the amount: 10.00 split between Ann, Ben and Cara is 3.34, 3.33 and 3.33.
43	
44	**Balances.** `balances` maps every member, in the group's member order, to what the group owes them (positive) or what they owe the group (negative). The payer of an expense is owed its amount, and each person in its `split` owes their share. A payment raises `from`'s balance and lowers `to`'s by its amount. The balances of a group always add up to 0.
45	
46	**Settling up.** `GET /groups/:id/settle-up` suggests the payments `[{from, to, amount}]` that would bring every balance to 0, without recording them. While someone owes money, the member who owes the most pays the member who is owed the most the smaller of those two amounts; on a tie, the member who comes first in the group's member order goes first.
47	
48	**Editing.** `PATCH` changes only the fields its body gives, each checked by the same rule as on `POST`; the others keep their value. Shares and balances always follow the expense as it is now.
49	
50	**Rules**
51	- `id` (group): 1 to 30 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting with a letter.
52	- `name` (group): a non-empty string of at most 100 characters.
53	- `members`: an array of 2 to 20 different member names. A member name is 1 to 30 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter; letter case matters.
54	- `description`: a non-empty string of at most 200 characters.
55	- `payer`, `from`, `to`: members of the group; `from` and `to` must differ.
56	- `amount`: a JSON number from 0.01 to 1000000 with at most 2 decimals, such as `12.5` or `4.35`. It is kept as whole cents and shown back as the same number.
57	- `split`: optional, a non-empty array of different members of the group. Without it the expense is split between every member, in the group's member order.
58	- Request bodies are JSON objects of at most 10 KB: a bigger body gets 413, a body that is not a JSON object gets 400. On every route except `POST /groups/:id/import`, unknown fields are ignored; the import refuses them.
59	- Every error is `{"error": "<message>"}`. An unknown route is 404 `{"error": "not found"}`. Fields are checked in the order the table lists them; the first bad one decides the 400 message.
60	
61	## Import
62	
63	`POST /groups/:id/import` records a list of expenses and payments for a group in one go: all of them, or none of them.
64	
65	The body is `{"entries": [...], "dry_run": <boolean>, "skip_recorded": <boolean>}`. `dry_run` and `skip_recorded` may be left out, and are then false. An entry is either an expense `{"type": "expense", "description", "payer", "amount", "split"}`, where `split` may be left out, or a payment `{"type": "payment", "from", "to", "amount"}`. Each field follows the same rule as on `POST /groups/:id/expenses` or `POST /groups/:id/payments`. A field counts as left out only when its key is absent: a present key is checked whatever its value, `null` included.
66	
67	After the 413 and non-object checks every route has, these checks run in order; the first that fails decides the reply, and a failed check saves nothing:
68	
69	1. Unknown group: 404 `{"error": "not found"}`.
70	2. 400 `{"error": "<message>"}`, the first that applies: `unknown field <name>` (any body field other than `entries`, `dry_run` and `skip_recorded`; the first one in `Object.keys` order), `entries must be an array of 1 to 50 items`, `dry_run must be true or false`, `skip_recorded must be true or false`.
71	3. 422 `{"error": "import rejected", "problems": [{"index", "rule"}, ...]}` when any entry breaks a rule: one item per such entry, sorted by `index` (its position in `entries`, from 0), with the first rule it breaks, in this order:
72	   - `not-an-object`: the entry is not a JSON object (null and arrays are not objects).
73	   - `bad-type`: `type` is not `"expense"` or `"payment"`.
74	   - `unknown-field`: a field its type does not take. An expense takes `type`, `description`, `payer`, `amount` and `split`; a payment takes `type`, `from`, `to` and `amount`.
75	   - Expense: `bad-description`, `bad-payer`, `bad-amount`, `bad-split`; then `duplicate` when an earlier entry that broke none of the rules above is an expense with the same payer, amount and description; then `already-recorded` when the group already has an expense with the same payer, amount and description. Descriptions are compared after `trim()` and `toLowerCase()`, amounts in cents; `split` is not compared. An earlier entry counts for `duplicate` even when it is itself `duplicate` or `already-recorded`, skipped or not.
76	   - Payment: `bad-from` (`from` is not a member), `bad-to` (`to` is not a member, or is `from`), `bad-amount`. Payments are never `duplicate` or `already-recorded`.
77	
78	   With `"skip_recorded": true`, an entry whose first broken rule is `already-recorded` is skipped instead of being a problem.
79	4. Success: 201 `{"expenses": [...], "payments": [...], "skipped": [...], "balances": {...}}`. Each entry that is not skipped becomes an expense or a payment exactly as the POST routes would make it, with consecutive ids of its kind in entry order, starting at the next id; the whole import is saved in one write. `expenses` and `payments` list the new ones in entry order, `skipped` the indexes of skipped entries in ascending order, and `balances` the group's balances after the import, as `GET /groups/:id/balances` gives them. When every entry is skipped, nothing is written.
80	
81	With `"dry_run": true`, the checks and error replies are the same, and a passing import gets the same body with status 200, but nothing is saved: the ids shown are the ones a real import would get now.
82	
83	## Layout
84	
85	- `server.mjs`: start-up, and the request loop: find the route, read the body, run the handler, save.
86	- `lib/http.mjs`: body reading, JSON replies, errors.
87	- `lib/routes.mjs`: route table.
88	- `lib/groups.mjs`, `lib/expenses.mjs`, `lib/import.mjs`: handlers. Handlers return a new store instead of changing the old one.
89	- `lib/validate.mjs`: input parsers; they throw `ValidationError` (400).
90	- `lib/ledger.mjs`: money maths on cents: shares, balances, and how expenses and payments are shown.
91	- `lib/store.mjs`: loading and atomic saving of the data file.
92	- `test/`: `node:test` suites; `helpers.mjs` starts the app on a free port with a temp data file.

I wrote `/root/bench-runs/h5-a984a158/test/import-checks.test.mjs` with 19 tests. All of them pass, and `npm test` passes in full (70 tests, 0 failed). I found no mismatch between the implementation and the README spec, and I did not touch `lib/`, `server.mjs` or the README.

The tests cover spec items 1–14, with one deviation from the spec: in the "different payer, amount or description" test, I added a per-pair suffix to each description. Without it, a passing pair would leave expenses behind and make the next pair "already-recorded". The checks themselves are unchanged.

The 400, 413 and 422 tests, and the dry-run test, run against a group with one expense and one payment already saved. At the end they check that the stored data is unchanged and that the next expense and payment ids are both 2.

Passing cases (the 1 and 50 item lists, the field boundaries, the not-duplicate pairs) assert the 201 status and the count of new expenses and payments, not the whole body. The success body is covered by the other coder's `test/import-success.test.mjs`.

I did not run a coverage tool.
